title: Sprint 6g: your own Tresorit drive in a work user's account, installed only when its signature holds

steps.say:
6g-0. What this walk needs, all on the laptop in your own account. Nothing is rented: the machine is the test VM 192.168.122.174, whose root takes the key ~/.claude/.ssh/claude_key, and a new user drive is made on it for your own drive.

- The wizard picks root's key from ~/.ssh. Link it there once, in a terminal of your own:

ln -s ~/.claude/.ssh/claude_key ~/.ssh/porelo-vm-admin && ln -s ~/.claude/.ssh/claude_key.pub ~/.ssh/porelo-vm-admin.pub

- Your Tresorit account (e-mail, password, the one-time code) and the name of one of your tresors.

Start this walk from ~/git/porelo-frontend with:

mkdir -p ~/.porelo/walk && cp doc/walks/20-sprint-6g-your-own-drive-on-a-machine.json ~/.porelo/walk/walk.json && PORELO_WALK=$HOME/.porelo/walk flutter run -d linux

Steps 6g-1 to 6g-14 were walked before you, up to Install Tresorit; the sign-in is yours. This panel moves on by itself when it sees what a step waits for; where you are ahead of it, click Next in this panel. Once all of this is in place, click Next here.

6g-1. In the rail click Machines, then Add a machine.

1. What to call it: vm-drive
2. Are you an administrator there? Yes: I may run commands as root there
3. How to reach it: Another user on a machine already prepared
4. The user that runs work there: drive
5. Click Next.

Expected: the wizard's step 1, The admin key root logs in with.

6g-2. Step 1, The admin key root logs in with: in Choose a key, pick porelo-vm-admin (another key may be chosen already; change it), then click Use this key. Expected: Root logs in with …/porelo-vm-admin, and drive will too.
6g-3. Click Next step. Expected: step 2, Where it is.
6g-4. Step 2, Where it is: Server name or IP address 192.168.122.174
6g-5. Click Try logging in as root. Where the machine's host key is shown for the first time, trust it. Expected: root is logged in.
6g-6. Click Next step. Expected: step 3, Preparing it.
6g-7. Click Show what it would do, and read the commands it shows.
6g-8. Click Run it as root. Expected: the setup script creates the user drive beside the others on the machine, with its own daemon and vault, and ends without an error.
6g-9. Click Next step. Expected: step 4, Reaching it as drive.
6g-10. The key drive logs in with stays A new one: ~/.ssh/porelo-vm-drive-drive. Click Set it up and connect. Expected: it answers and can be watched.
6g-11. Click Next step. Expected: step 5, The vault.

6g-12. Click Open a terminal to make the vault and type a new vault passphrase twice, Enter after each. Expected: nothing you type is shown, the terminal ends, and below it: The vault is there, and it opens with the passphrase typed.

6g-13. Click Next step. Expected: step 6, Your own drive (optional): the text that it is optional, and Install Tresorit for drive as the only thing offered; no field asks anything yet. Next step from there would go on with nothing of Tresorit installed; do not click it there.

6g-14. Click Install Tresorit for drive. Expected: Tresorit's client is installed for drive, from an installer its signature vouched for, and runs; then a field Tresorit e-mail. Failure signs: did not pass its check on the machine, so nothing of it ran, with openssl's words, or holds no CA with the pinned fingerprint: then nothing ran, and the installer Tresorit serves no longer matches the pin.
6g-15. Type your Tresorit e-mail into Tresorit e-mail.
6g-16. Click Open a terminal to sign in. In that terminal Tresorit asks its password without echo, then the one-time code. Expected after the terminal ends: Signed in as <your e-mail>.
6g-17. Type the name of one of your tresors and click Sync it. Expected: <tresor> syncs into ~/Tresorit/<tresor> for drive alone; root and the other users on the machine cannot read it.
6g-18. Tell me in this panel what differed. I take the drive off and remove the user drive and the machine vm-drive afterwards.
